attribution_hierarchy: 1. Randomized Controlled Trials / Holdouts (Highest Causal Reliability)
3. Strong Quasi-Experimental Designs (Regression Discontinuity / Synthetic Controls)
5. Platform-Reported Attribution (Lowest Causal Reliability / Directional Only)

attribution_methods.scope: First-touch and last-touch referral logging via UTM parameters
attribution_methods.use_case: Operational routing and channel traffic composition analysis.
attribution_methods.assumptions: Assumes recorded touchpoint is correlated with visit; does NOT establish causal incrementality.

attribution_methods.scope: In-platform conversion reporting (e.g. ad network pixel tracking)
attribution_methods.use_case: Campaign delivery optimization and automated algorithmic pacing.
attribution_methods.assumptions: Known platform self-attribution bias; must never be reported as incrementality proof.

attribution_methods.scope: Holdout cohorts and randomized creative delivery splits
attribution_methods.use_case: Determining true causal net-new developer acquisition lift.
attribution_methods.assumptions: Requires stable control group without cross-contamination.

attribution_methods.scope: Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) when multi-channel spend scale is reached
attribution_methods.use_case: Macro channel allocation and diminishing returns analysis.
attribution_methods.assumptions: Requires sufficient time-series variance and spend magnitude; currently UNKNOWN/NOT_APPLICABLE.

causal_discipline_rules: Never claim platform-reported conversions represent true incremental lift.
Never assert Multi-Touch Attribution (MTA) represents causal truth.
